card.$description: Card. Component tokens are the customisation point for one component. They reference SEMANTIC tokens — by token path when the value is theme-agnostic, or through the semantic CSS variable (--qx-color-*) when it is theme-varying, so one declaration covers both themes. A component token must never reference another component's tokens. Everything lives under the `component.*` namespace: the shadcn bridge already publishes leaves named `input`, `card`, `radius` and so on, and a token path cannot be both a leaf and a group.

background-elevated.$description: Fill of the `elevated` variant. Identical to the default surface in light; one step lighter in dark, where elevation is carried by lightness as much as by shadow.

ring.$description: The card's 1px boundary, and the colour of its internal dividers (a header `border-b`, the footer rule). Painted as a real border rather than a box-shadow ring so the boundary survives forced-colours mode, where box-shadow is stripped; the name predates that switch and is kept so existing overrides still apply.

border-hover.$description: Boundary of an `interactive` card under the pointer. Decorative feedback paired with the hover lift — never the only signal, so it does not need 3:1.

border-selected.$description: Boundary of a `selected` card, doubled to 2px with a matching ring. The brand border role is designed at 3:1 or better against every surface, so selection passes non-text contrast instead of relying on a tint.

footer-background.$description: The band behind a card's footer actions — one quiet step off the card surface in both themes.

elevation-hover.$description: Lift of an `interactive` card under the pointer. Static cards do not lift: a hover response on a surface that does nothing is a false affordance.

elevation-elevated.$description: Resting shadow of the `elevated` variant — one step above a default card, for the one surface on a page that has to stand forward (a summary panel, a floating detail). Separate from elevation-hover so the two can be tuned independently.
